To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

rifampicin increases the rate of β- and β′-subunit synthesis in a heteroploid Escherichia colistrain, that the increased rate persists after rifampicin is removed, and that the increased rate of synthesis is not accompanied by an increase in the rate of transcription of the ββ’ operon.
rifampicin increases β and β′ levels 1.6-fold and that the rate of ββ′ synthesis is not autoregulated in E. coli.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the mechanism by which the synthesis of β and β subunits is controlled in the cell, and we conclude that the mechanism of control is not by a feedback inhibition of their synthesis by the subunits themselves.
the regulation of the synthesis of the β and β′ polypeptides of Escherichia Coli RNA polymerase, which are coded for by the β and β’ operons.
the synthesis of the β and β′ polypeptides of RNA polymerase and the control of their concentration in the cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence to support the hypothesis that the rate of ββ′ operons is regulated by autorepression in the cell.
there is no evidence for autorepression of either the β or β′ subunits in the ββ′-operon in Eschericia coli.
the β and β′ operon in E. coli is not subject to autoregulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is no evidence for autorepression of β or β′ in Escherichiacoli.
the ββ′ promoter does not appear to be subject to autogenous regulation.
the ββ′ subunits do not regulate their own synthesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the β and β′ operon is not autorepressed in E. coli.
the ββ′ promoter is a strong, constitutive promoter, that is not autorepressed.
the concentration of RNA polymerase subunits is regulated by the rate of transcription of their genes, and not by the rate of translation of the mRNAs.
